summary: Ram Shankar Tripathi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as Reader and Head of Buddhist Philosophy at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1977-1998) and Dean of Śabdavidyā at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2001).

Ram Sharan Sharma was a historian and Indologist who earned his PhD at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He was a professor at Patna University (1958-1973) and the University of Delhi (1973-1985), and founded the Indian Council of Historical Research.

Rama Mishra Shastri was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, where he served as Professor (attested 1882-1889) and assistant Professor of Sāṅkhya (attested 1914).

Rama Nath Sharma is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Raghunatha Sharma and Ramaprasada Tripathi, completing his PhD at the University of Rochester. He taught at Allahabad (1962-1966), Rochester (1971-1976), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (from 1976).

Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Martin Haug, at the University of Mumbai, and at Göttingen (PhD). He was a professor at Elphinstone College, Deccan College, and served as Vice Chancellor of the University of Mumbai.

Ramanatha Dikshita was an Indologist. He worked in the Sādhulāla research section at Sarasvati Bhavana (attested 1944) and served as Head of the Veda Department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1970).

Ramaprasad Chanda was an archaeologist and Indologist educated at Scottish Church College. He worked at the Archaeological Survey of India (1917-1919), lectured at the University of Calcutta, and served as Superintendent of the Archaeological Section at the Indian Museum (1921-1932).
Ramaprasada Tripathi was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1976 and 2001) and taught Rama Nath Sharma.

Ramaranjan Mukherji was an Indologist who completed his BA and PhD at the University of Calcutta and a Doctor of Literature at Jadavpur University. He served as department head at Jadavpur and vice chancellor of Burdwan and Rabindra Bharati Universities.

Ramchandra B. Athavale was an Indologist. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat Vidyapith, L. D. Arts College (attested 1938), and S. L. U. Arts and H. & P. Thakore Commerce College for Women (attested 1938).

Ramchandra Narayan Dandekar was an Indologist who studied at the University of Mumbai and Heidelberg University. He taught at Fergusson College, served as Professor and Dean at Savitribai Phule Pune University, and was Honorary Secretary of Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Ramesh Chandra Negi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He has worked at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies as a Research Assistant (attested 2001-2004) and Associate Professor (attested 2026).

Ramesh Chandra Majumdar was an Indian historian who earned his doctorate from the University of Calcutta. He taught at Calcutta and was Professor, Dean, and Provost at the University of Dhaka, later serving as Principal at Banaras Hindu University.

Ramesh Shankar Gupte was an Indologist and historian who headed the Department of History and Ancient Indian Culture at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University (attested 1967) and served as a visiting lecturer at Wake Forest University, Salem College, and Winston-Salem State University.

Ramin Etesami is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Lobsang Jamspal and Krishna Ghosh Della Santina (attested 2015).
Ramkrishna Bhattacharya was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Calcutta (around 1968-1970) and held a post at Ananda Mohan College (around 1972-2007).
Ramon Prats is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Himalayan and Inner Asian Resources (attested 1999) and Pompeu Fabra University (attested 2017).
Randall Studstill is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied under teachers Steven D. Goodman and Richard Payne, who was his doctoral supervisor.

Randy J. LaPolla is a linguist and sinologist who studied at the University of California, Berkeley under James Alan Matisoff. He served as Professor at the City University of Hong Kong (around 1996-1999) and joined Beijing Normal University, Zhuhai (2021).

Rangama Chandawimala is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin and Kakkapalliye Anuruddha, and became an Associate Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).
